title: Email testing: Mailinator, Gmail Tester and confirmation flows

videos.script: Sign up for almost anything and an e-mail arrives with a link. {{flow}} That link is a small secret. It expires, it can be replaced, and an old one should stop working. {{rules}} Those rules are where e-mail goes wrong. The sending is the easy part. {{catcher}} A test environment never sends mail to real people. It catches every message, somewhere a tester can read it. In boxoffice, that place is the outbox. {{signup}} You sign up, read the message in the outbox, and confirm the account. {{resend}} Then you ask for a second link and try the first one. It still works, and the requirement says it should not. {{expiry}} You also meet a test that cannot fail, and learn how to spot one. {{hosted}} Last come the inboxes for applications that have no outbox. One you run yourself, one that is public, and a real one that a test reads. {{close}} And you see why a public inbox never gets real data.
